lesson_metadata.subject: Math
misconceptions: Students may think that borrowing means taking money from someone else.
Students may struggle with understanding the concept of borrowing in subtraction.

lesson_flow.title: Introduction to Subtraction with Borrowing
lesson_flow.description: Introduce the concept of subtraction with borrowing using real-life examples.
lesson_flow.content: Imagine you have 72 rupees in your piggy bank and you want to subtract 47 rupees from it. But, you don't have enough rupees to subtract 47 from 72. What can you do?

lesson_flow.title: Borrowing in Subtraction
lesson_flow.description: Explain the concept of borrowing in subtraction.
lesson_flow.content: When we subtract a bigger number from a smaller number, we need to borrow some quantity from our neighbour. Let's learn how to do it.

lesson_flow.title: Practice Exercise
lesson_flow.description: Provide practice exercises for students to apply subtraction with borrowing.
lesson_flow.content: Practice subtracting bigger numbers from smaller numbers using borrowing.

lesson_flow.title: Real-Life Application
lesson_flow.description: Provide real-life examples of subtraction with borrowing.
lesson_flow.content: Let's learn how to apply subtraction with borrowing in real-life situations.

lesson_flow.title: Conclusion
lesson_flow.description: Summarize the concept of subtraction with borrowing.
lesson_flow.content: Now, you know how to subtract bigger numbers from smaller numbers using borrowing. Practice it regularly to become a master!

Take some rupees from your piggy bank

interaction_plan.question: What is the main idea of subtraction with borrowing?

Borrowing some quantity from our neighbour
